episodes.195312: A fairly weak shortwave slipped by the forecast region to the north, but provided sufficient  synoptic support to yield scattered high-based convective development, and some convection resulted in severe wind gusts.
episodes.195612: More heavy rain occurred due to plenty of moisture and lift around the Blue Ridge Mountains of central Virginia. The ground was already saturated due to previous rainfall, so this led to more instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.196626: One report of severe thunderstorm wind gust in Clark County.
episodes.196769: The end of September featured a strong Category 4 Hurricane Helene, which made landfall in the Florida Big Bend region on September 26th. After sailing through the Mississippi Valley, Helene quickly deviated its track to the west-northwest as it began to pivot around an increasingly cut off upper level low disturbance positioned over Kentucky, and became post-tropical in the process. This brought forth the start of impacts to West Virginia on the 27th, especially across west-central parts of the state, with strong to damaging wind gusts and locally heavy rainfall.||Wind gusts of 50 to 60 miles per hour were observed frequently across southwest West Virginia, with multiple areas of downed trees and power lines in McDowell, Wayne, and Wood Counties on September 27th. The strongest wind gust observed in the state occurred at the Huntington Airport in Cabell County, recording a gust of 70 miles per hour just after 12:00 that afternoon. There was also an instance of flash flooding in Jackson County, where a local creek rose out of its banks and spilled onto the local road. This was from the locally heavy rainfall that was associated with Helene, which yielded much needed moisture to the state after a summer filled with a historic drought.||Additional rounds of showers continued to impact West Virginia from September 28th to October 1st as the lingering remnants of Helene were absorbed by the stationary upper level disturbance, and would only come to an end with the help of a crossing cold front on October 2nd. However, no additional impacts were caused by Helene after the 29th across West Virginia.
episodes.197106: The remnants of Tropical Storm Helene brought widespread heavy rain to the region that led to river flooding and flash flooding in the state of West Virginia.

events.narrative: A river gauge located on the Shenandoah River at Front Royal reach minor flood stage (12ft) with crest of 12.35 feet. At 12 feet, backwater flooding begins to creep up Luray Avenue toward the railroad trestle. A riverside parking area at the end of Luray Avenue is flooded.

The River Gauge on the Shenandoah River near Millville, WV reached minor flood stage (10ft) with a peak crest of 11.16 feet. At 10 feet, parts of Bloomery Road and John Rissler Road are flooded near Bloomery, West Virginia. Once these roads flood, access to homes is impaired but the homes themselves are not in any danger of flooding. Moulton Park and the Millville boat launch are also flooded. At 11 feet,  a small portion of Wilt Road (County Road 9/8) begins to flood. Water also begins to flow over Millville Dam.
